rules.description: A root-owned SUID binary is writable by all users, allowing direct replacement of its executable content.
rules.exploit: Overwrite the binary with attacker-controlled code (e.g. a shell spawn); it will run as root when executed.

rules.description: A SUID binary is owned by a user other than root, granting that user's identity rather than root when executed.
rules.exploit: Execute the binary to gain the file owner's identity, which may enable further lateral movement or a separate privilege escalation chain.

rules.description: A SUID binary is located in a user-writable or non-standard location, suggesting it may be a planted or custom binary rather than a distro package.
rules.exploit: Inspect the binary directly (strings, ltrace, or disassembly) to determine what it does and whether it can be leveraged for privilege escalation.
